severity_name: SEVERE SLOP WARNING — INFORMATION INTEGRITY ADVISORY
headline: SEVERE SLOP WARNING: INDUSTRIAL-SCALE INFLUENCE FRONT RETOOLS WITH CHEAP AI SLOP AS PROPAGANDA OPERATIONS DISCOVER THEY NO LONGER NEED WRITERS, TRANSLATORS, OR, INCREASINGLY, FACTS TO FLOOD FIVE REGIONS AT ONCE
advisory: The Service is tracking a broad, well-funded low-pressure system in which large influence campaigns have quietly swapped human copywriters for generative models, cutting the marginal cost of a misleading article to roughly nothing. Residents are advised that the volume of persuasion has increased while the number of persuaders has not; a single operator may now produce in an hour what once required a floor of staff and a coffee budget. Cross-reference before you share. When a story arrives fully formed, faintly foreign in its cadence, and eager for your outrage, treat it as weather rather than news.

regional_outlook.conditions: Heavy circulation of fabricated 'local concern' posts drifting downstream from pages created eleven days ago. Shares outpace reads by a factor the Delta has not seen since the last election cycle.
Persistent gusts of coordinated reply traffic, all arriving within the same ninety seconds and all agreeing with unusual enthusiasm. Visibility poor; sincerity nil.
Standing water of counterfeit news domains ranking above the outlets they impersonate. Residents wading in are advised to check the masthead before drinking.
A newly saturated wetland where 'hometown' outlets with civic-sounding names publish stories no local resident recognizes. Datelines fabricated; weather report probably also fabricated.
Rising tide of forwarded chain-articles, each 'just something I saw,' each generated by the same silent machine upstream.

specimen.status: Invasive; breeding faster than it can be catalogued.
specimen.habitat: Domains with reassuring civic names — the Herald, the Sentinel, the County Ledger — none of which have a county, a herald, or a sentinel.
specimen.field_marks: Trustworthy serif typeface; an 'About Us' page describing a newsroom that does not exist; a staff of bylines that share one prose style and no birthdays. Publishes forty 'local' stories a day for towns it cannot locate on a map.
specimen.call: BREAKING: Community Outraged Over Decision — Here's What Residents Are Saying (residents unavailable for comment, as they are hypothetical)
specimen.confusion_species: Easily mistaken for a genuine struggling local paper, which it is engineered to resemble. Tell them apart by the details: the real one misspells a name and prints a correction; the Gazette never errs, never corrects, and has never once covered a school board meeting that actually happened.

spotter_tip: If an outlet you've never heard of has strong opinions about your town but cannot name a single street in it, you are not reading the news — you are being weathered on.
tomorrow: Influence front lingers overnight; expect scattered 'grassroots' precipitation and a persistent haze of manufactured consensus by midmorning.

confirmed_sighting.report: Researchers report that some of the largest online propaganda and influence campaigns are now relying on cheap, AI-generated 'slop' to mass-produce misleading content at scale. The Service notes, without surprise, that the barrier to industrial dishonesty is now roughly the price of an API call.
